title: finding(components): `OPT_IN_OPERATORS`' doc block says the other two vocabularies have no case-insensitive contains — false on spec 17.4.0, and its stated exit condition is already met while the blocker moved to a missing alias row
body:
Path: none | docblock 对两个词表的断言为假 | 纯文档措辞

`OPT_IN_OPERATORS`' doc block in `packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx` states a fact that is **no longer true**, and its own stated exit condition is **already met** — while the operator stays unreachable for a different reason the prose never moved to.

Seat-verified at source on `origin/main` `aced50d2e`, `:171` verbatim:

> The other two vocabularies have **no case-insensitive contains at all**, so offering it everywhere is the exact hazard objectui#4023 was held blocked over …

and `:200`–`:202`, the exit condition it names:

> The lasting fix for both families is upstream — **the view and AST vocabularies gaining the operator** — at which point the entry below is deleted, the parity test flips it back on by itself, and the operator becomes ordinary.

## Measured against the installed spec — ⛔ relayed and attributed, ⛔ not re-run by this seat

The objectui#9559 dev measured on `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0**, with controls in the same command:

- `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` **contains `icontains`**;
- `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` **contains `ilike` and `icontains`**;
- the sibling claim about `exists` — 「both sets have ZERO members matching `/exist/`」 — is **still TRUE**, and its control (the Mongo dialect yielding the `$exists` token) fires, so the instrument is live and only the case-insensitive sentence is false.

⚠️ This seat did ⛔ **not** re-run those set reads: the shared checkout has no `node_modules`. What this seat verified is the two sentences above, at those line numbers.

## ⭐ Why it still cannot be offered — the blocker MOVED and the prose did not

`normalizeFilterOperator` has **no alias row** for the camelCase spelling `containsCaseInsensitive`. ⇒ the blocker went from 「the vocabularies have no such member」 to 「the member exists under `icontains` and nothing maps this id onto it」, and the doc block still tells the next reader the first story.

## Class (b) — it violates a declared contract of this repo's own

AGENTS.md #9: 「when you declare something verified, point at the instrument that re-derives it — the script, the gate, the test — and never write down its answer」. This block writes down an answer. ⭐ The instrument it should point at **exists**: `plugin-list`'s `list-offered-operator-expressible-parity.test.ts` forces the offered set to EQUAL the expressible set in both directions, and the objectui#9559 dev read its assertions and confirms it would catch an actual deletion of the opt-in entry. ⇒ this is a **stale claim**, ⛔ not an unguarded trap.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT settle

Whether the remedy is to rename the dropdown id to `icontains`, to add the alias row upstream, or to rewrite the sentence and leave the id opt-in. ⚠️ That is entangled with objectui#9559's ruling (now in the decision box, on whether objectui's mirror should derive from the spec) — ⇒ whoever takes this reads that card first, and ⛔ neither should be dispatched while the other is unruled.

## Dedupe words

`filter-builder OPT_IN_OPERATORS containsCaseInsensitive icontains stale` · `no case-insensitive contains at all false` · `exit condition already met` · `normalizeFilterOperator missing alias row` · `AGENTS #9 write down the answer`
